summary: A. P. Buddhadatta (1887–1962) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a Pali tutor at Ananda College and was attested as a member of Kalyanavamsa Nikaya in 1923.
A. S. Gadre worked in the fields of Indology and history and archaeology. In 1944, he was attested as Director of Archaeology for Baroda State and its Archaeology Department.

A. S. Ramanatha Ayyar (d. 1941) was an Indology and history and archaeology scholar. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1918–1941), as Superintendent of the Travancore Archaeology Department (1922), and in Thiruvithamkoor (~1924–1934).

A. V. Williams Jackson (1862–1937) was an Indology, Iranian, and linguistics scholar. He earned his PhD at Columbia, also studying at Halle under Geldner and Pischel. He was a professor of English literature (1883–1890) and professor (1895–1935) at Columbia.
A.-Ferdinand Hérold (1865–1940) worked in Indology. He studied at the École Nationale des Chartes (~1886–1890) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1888–1892), earning a Licensié-ès-lettres.
Aalekhya Malladi specializes in religious studies and Indology. She completed a PhD at Emory University in 2022 and was appointed assistant professor at McGill University in 2023.

Aaron P. Proffitt specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a PhD from the University of Michigan (~2009–2015) under Micah L. Auerback and became assistant professor of Japanese Studies at the University at Albany, SUNY, around 2017.
Abaji Vishnu Kathavate was an Indologist. He succeeded Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).

Abanindranath Tagore (1871–1951) was an Indology and history and archaeology scholar. He studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College and University, and the Government College of Art and Craft, and held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1921–1929).

Abdur Rehman is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He earned a PhD at Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Peshawar (attested 1988).

Abel Bergaigne (1838–1888) worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Armand Hauvette-Besnault. He held posts at the EPHE (from 1868), the University of Paris (1877), and the Sorbonne as professor (from 1885).

Abel Hovelacque (1843–1896) was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Honoré-Joseph Chavée (~1864–1867). He served as Professor of Linguistics (from 1876) and Director (from 1891) at the École d'Anthropologie.

Abhijit Mandal is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He earned an MA from Ramakrishna Mission Vidyamandira (2011–2013) and a PhD from the University of Calcutta (2014–2018), becoming Assistant Professor at Cooch Behar Panchanan Barma University in 2016.
Abhimanyu Rao is an Indologist who studied under Deepak Dabral and held a post at Shiv Nadar School.

Abhiraj Rajendra Mishra (b. 1943) is an Indologist who studied under Rāmbhadrācārya. He headed the Sanskrit department at Himachal Pradesh University (~1980–2003), was a visiting professor at the University of Indonesia (~1987–1989), and served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~2004–2005).

Abidin İtil (1910–1980) was an Indology scholar who earned a PhD at Ankara University (~1940–1944) under Walter Ruben. He taught Sanskrit from 1936 at Ankara University, later serving as assistant (1943–1946) and department head and professor (~1954–1975).
Abigail I. MacBain is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned an MA at McMaster University (attested 2008) and held a post at the University of Edinburgh in 2022.

Abigail Leach (1855–1918) studied classics and Indology at Radcliffe, Vassar (AB, AM ~1883–1885), and Leipzig. She taught at Boston Latin Academy (1880–1883), chaired Greek at Vassar (1889), and served as president of the Society for Classical Studies (1898–1900).

Abirlal Gangopadhyay is an Indologist who completed an Uttaramadhyamā at Ramakrishna Math Vivekananda Veda Vidyalaya, a BA at RKMVERI, an MA at Jadavpur University, and a PhD at the University of Hyderabad (2018–2023).

Abraham Anthony Fokker (1862–1927) worked in linguistics and earned a PhD at Leiden University (~1889–1894). He taught Malay at the University of Amsterdam and was a professor at the University of Indonesia.
